top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation of a mass in the breast, mobile with no skin involvement, and axillary lymph nodes not palpable, along with imaging findings of a lobulated, well-defined mass on mammogram and a solid, hypoechoic, well-circumscribed mass on ultrasound, are consistent with Invasive Ductal Carcinoma. The excisional biopsy results showing invasive adenocarcinoma, polygonal cells with well-defined borders, and solid, lobular, acinar and papillary areas further support this diagnosis. Additionally, the tumor's positive staining for estrogen receptors (ER) and negative staining for progesterone receptors (PgR) are also characteristic of Invasive Ductal Carcinoma.
